description: A monophonic bass voice: a sawtooth through a four-pole ladder filter, with a separate phase-modulated sub layer an octave below

params.text: Shifts both layers in whole octaves, from -4 to +4
Sets the filter cutoff from 42Hz up to 3276Hz, before the envelope adds to it
Raises the feedback around the ladder filter, up to 3.35 times
Blends in the sub layer; at zero the output is the upper layer alone
Sets how far the filter envelope opens the cutoff, adding up to 2600Hz on top of the FILTER setting
Sets how long the note falls away for once the gate drops, 0.03 to 4 seconds, and lengthens the filter envelope along with it
Adds warm asymmetric saturation at the output with make-up gain behind it, so the level stays roughly steady as it is raised
Detunes the upper layer by -100 to +100 cents, leaving the sub layer at the written pitch

inputs.text: Volt-per-octave pitch for both layers, added to the OCTAVE knob
Above 1V it opens the voice and restarts the filter envelope; the note decays once the voltage falls below 0.1V
0-10V adding up to a third of the ENV AMT range on top of the knob, with an 8ms rise and a 40ms fall put on it first
Offsets FILTER, 10V covering the knob's full travel
Offsets ENV AMT, 10V covering the knob's full travel
Offsets SUB, 10V covering the knob's full travel
Offsets DRIVE, 10V covering the knob's full travel
Offsets DECAY, 10V covering the knob's full range of 0.03 to 4 seconds
Offsets RES, 10V covering the knob's full travel

outputs.text: The finished voice, both layers mixed, saturated and DC blocked, ±5V

notes: nothing comes out until a gate arrives. Patch a gate to GATE, and a pitch to V/OCT if the OCTAVE knob alone is not enough
the sub layer tracks V/OCT and OCTAVE one octave down but ignores TUNE, so detuning the upper layer beats against a sub that stays in tune
